newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German machine maker Sket to be broken up.
newsitem.headline: East German machine maker Sket to be broken up.

text.p: Sket GmbH, the former East Germany's biggest heavy machinery group, said on Thursday it would undergo massive restructuring and shed a third of its workforce.
Managing director Werner Kirchgaesser told reporters that it was necessary to spin off Sket's steel rolling mills, cable and wire plants, and oil and production divisions into separate companies.
Kirchgaesser, formerly head of Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, was speaking after a meeting of the loss-making east German machinery maker's supervisory board.
Breaking up the company into independent parts would lead to the loss of 600 jobs from a workforce of 1,850.
Management said the restructuring plan could bring the company back into profitability by the end of 1998. It expects a loss of around 190 million marks this year.
The supervisory board will make a final decision about the restructuring on October 14.
